text.p: SME - President Michal Kovac has said he does not expect the current government of Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar to be able and willing to implement democratic changes required by the European Union.

- The government on Tuesday approved a 10 percent increase in energy prices for corporate customers. The government rejected an economics ministry proposal to increase energy prices for private customers by 20 percent.

- The cabinet said on Tuesday it fully agreed with his Premier Meciar's remarks that U.S. ambassador to Slovakia Ralph Johnson exceeded his authority when he commented on why Slovakia was not invited to the first wave of NATO enlargement.

- The Constitutional Court is expected to rule by the end of this weak on an appeal by Frantisek Gaulieder, a former deputy for the ruling Movement for the Democratic Slovakia (HZDS), against his expulsion from the parliament last autumn.
NARODNA OBRODA - Recent heavy rains and floodings are estimated to have caused financial damages of around 2.33 billion crowns. Around half of the damage is in the agricultural sector.
- Slovakia's retail sales totalled 27.5 billion crowns in May, an increase of 5.4 percent over the same month last year.
- JAS Bardejov, one of the largest Slovak shoe producers, said it may have to lay off half of its 4,200 employees if the company does not find financial sources for restructuring.
PRAVDA - State-run Slovak Railways (ZSR) are expected to post a net loss of 2.0 to 2.5 billion crowns in the first half of this year.
- Overall investment in railway infrastructure is expected to total some 100 billion crowns by the year 2010. The main priorities are recostruction of the south-north and east-west corridors.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Water level on the river Danube started to fall on Tuesday. The only problematic river is now the Morava on the Czech-Slovak border where rescue forces have prepared evacuation of several vilages.
